title: Ethanol-induced activation of adenine nucleotide turnover. Evidence for a role of acetate
population: Five healthy volunteers aged 21 to 32 years on a purine-free diet in a clinical research centre
funder: This work was supported by grants from U. S. Public Health Service 2 R01AM 19674, 5MORR42, and 5P60AM20572 and the Social Security Investigational Program of Spain.
result: Intravenous ethanol, 0.1 mmol/kg per min for 1 h, raised plasma acetate from 0.04 to 0.08 mM and urinary oxypurines to 316% of baseline; urinary radioactivity from the [8-14C]adenine-labelled nucleotide pool rose to 128%. Activation of acetate to acetyl-CoA (acetate + ATP to acetyl-AMP + PPi; acetyl-AMP + CoA to acetyl-CoA + AMP) consumes 2 high-energy phosphates per acetate; the authors conclude that acetate metabolism contributes to the increased urate production after ethanol, a small part of the AMP entering purine degradation.
